findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached Hungarian endpoint mean-squared-distance and native endpoint VJP, so no affinity-head derivative or extra model forward is available as evidence.

The observed score window is [0.0, 0.5] with 50 observed score times at 0.01 spacing, and the curve support is [0.0, 0.49]; recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so no observed affinity label is available to validate any coordinate contrast against final affinity.

Continuous contrast features are represented in predicted endpoint world coordinates and are only observed-node linear fits: extrapolation is not allowed, polynomial fits are not accepted, and relative node RMSE ranges from about 0.29 to 0.78 across the first six landmark features, so these curves are descriptive interpolations rather than validated absolute reward targets.

The inspected landmark contrast curves show sign changes and rate reversals within the observed window: landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes with first_rate_z about +9.3 and last_rate_z about -10.0; landmark_00_local_dx has 6 sign changes with first_rate_z about -17.5 and last_rate_z about +8.1; landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes with first_rate_z about -72.4 and last_rate_z about +5.5; landmark_00_local_dz has 10 sign changes; landmark_00_local_cxx has 6 sign changes; landmark_00_local_cyy has 4 sign changes. This supports a time-conditioned contrast rule over a constant rule within the observed support.

Several of the inspected curves carry strong sign conflicts (landmark_00_local_dx: 9; landmark_00_local_dz: 7; landmark_00_local_dy: 4; landmark_00_local_cxx: 2; landmark_00_soft_mass: 1; landmark_00_local_cyy: 1), so the direction of the contrast is not stable across the observed window and a single signed direction cannot be asserted from these rows alone.

hypotheses.falsifier: A constant-sign rule matches or exceeds the time-conditioned rule on observed-node fit fidelity across the window.
hypotheses.observable: observed-node contrast sign and rate of landmark coordinate features
hypotheses.scope: observed score window [0.0, 0.5], predicted endpoint world coordinates
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned contrast rule that follows the observed-node sign and rate changes of the landmark coordinate features will track the observed contrast better than a constant-sign rule over the window [0.0, 0.5].

hypotheses.falsifier: Local displacement/curvature features show fewer sign changes and conflicts than soft_mass under the same fit method.
hypotheses.scope: first six landmark features in continuous_trends
hypotheses.statement: Landmark local displacement and curvature features (dx, dy, dz, cxx, cyy) carry more sign instability than the soft-mass feature, so they should be treated as lower-priority directional evidence.

limitations: Recorded affinities were removed and replaced by an equal score prior, so no observed affinity label is available to validate coordinate contrasts against final predicted target affinity.

Only the first six continuous_trends rows were read; the remaining 194 curve features, branch_adjusted, endpoint_effects, increment_effects, joint_diagnostics, regional_effects, survival_effects, turnover_accounting, lineage_support and information_audit tables were not inspected in this turn.
No decoded terminal labels or current-study outcome data are supplied, so last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit.

Continuous contrast curves are observed-node linear interpolations with extrapolation disallowed and polynomial fits rejected; they are not absolute reward targets and no extrapolation beyond [0.0, 0.49] is supported.
No covariance, intact-conformation or mode diagnostics were read, so coherent joint coordinate patterns versus isolated marginals cannot be compared from the evidence inspected.
